Chapter Five: Rediscovering Purpose and the Will to Compete Again.
Coming out from under the shadow of illness isn’t a straightforward journey. It moves slowly, sometimes with steps forward, sometimes with setbacks. Your body starts to heal, sure, but your mind? It can get stuck replaying memories of pain, of feeling vulnerable—especially if competition used to be at the very core of who you are.
So, what do you do when you’re finally ready to ask, “What comes next?”
Those first rides back on the bike felt awkward. The same routines that used to feel like second nature suddenly seemed strange. Muscles didn’t respond the way they once did. Simple training rides demanded everything you had. It was frustrating—sometimes even infuriating—to bump up against those new limits set by illness. But, underneath all that, something new started to grow.
It wasn’t just about getting back to where you were. It was about showing yourself, and maybe everyone else, that surviving could actually be the start of something new. Not the end of the story.
Family, friends, and the cycling community? They made all the difference. Their belief in you helped balance out the times you doubted yourself. Their encouragement was a lifeline—a reminder that you’re not in this alone. And your medical team stayed in your corner, checking on your progress and guiding you through the tough patches.
Little by little, you felt your strength return. The number of miles you could handle started to climb. With every ride, possibilities seemed a little closer. Of course, it wasn’t all smooth sailing. There were setbacks—days when illness or fatigue crept back in, moments when you just wanted to give up. But each challenge was a chance to dig a little deeper.
The lessons you picked up during treatment—things like patience, humility, and knowing when to ask for help—became the tools you leaned on most in recovery.
And eventually, the return to competition meant so much more than chasing a personal best. It became a symbol—a sign of hope, proof of resilience. Every victory, no matter how small, was sweeter because of the struggle it took to get there.
Going through illness stripped away any illusion of being invincible. But in its place, it left you with something even more important: a deeper appreciation for just how fragile—and beautiful—life can be.
